text:
morgan: CI perf unit failed for PR #14900 on the microbench suite — batcher_affinity_test shows ~12% tail latency regression. cc @anish @tess :thinking_face:

anish: saw the alert. starting a quick bisect. failing threshold is +0.12 relative. CI job: https://ci.redwood/sys/job/14900/perf-diff

tess: reproduced locally on my T4 dev box, tail latency is 1.15x. flamegraph points to scheduler wait / batch composition hotspot. rough profile:```
  scheduler_thread   45.3%  // time in batch composition loop
  kv_cache_lookup    20.1%
  copy_worker        10.2%
  other              24.4%
```

samir: this smells like the new prefetch/sampler changes from PR 14888 — that altered the bucket selection semantics. commit: https://git.redwood/commit/9a7f2c3. I can run a targeted microbench against that commit.

morgan: thanks. bisect quick run shows commit 9a7f2c3 correlates with the regression. repro steps I used:
```
git checkout 9a7f2c3
cargo bench --bench microbench -- batcher_affinity_test --release
# compare with HEAD~1
```

ci-bot: artifacts for failed run: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/14900/perf/diff.json and perf flamegraph: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/14900/perf/flame.svg

laura: quick analysis: sampler now allows a larger prefetch window which increases the chance of grouping long-seqlen requests with short ones, creating head-of-line blocking and uneven batch sizes. two quick mitigations: revert the sampler change, or enforce a max-bucket-size cap when composing batches.

tess: if we revert, we should add a unit microbench that synthesizes skewed seq length distributions to catch this in CI. I'll open an eval test after a revert.

morgan: I'm going to roll back the canary and mark PR 14900 as rollout-blocker. pushing a revert patch now. @samir can you prepare a narrow fix (max-bucket cap) as an alternative?

samir: on it. I'll prototype a fix that limits per-bucket inflight size and add a histogram test for batch size distribution. will send PR in ~1h. :wrench:

laura: also adding a perf unit that asserts tail P99 doesn't increase more than 3% for a set of skewed workloads. should stop regressions like this slipping through.

morgan: good plan. thanks everyone, keeping this thread for updates. once samir's fix lands we'll re-run the microbench regression job and un-block the rollout. :thumbsup:
